summary: Paul David Devanandan was a religious studies scholar. Educated at Nizam College, Presidency University, Pacific School of Religion, and Yale University, he taught at Jaffna College, United Theological College (1932–1949), and directed the Christian Institute for the Study of Religion and Society (1956).

Paul David Numrich is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Michigan in 1992. In 2006, he held posts at Loyola University Chicago and the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus.

Paul Debes was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Nyanatiloka Mahathera from 1931 to 1932. He founded the Buddhistisches Seminar in 1948, the Deutsche Buddhistische Gesellschaft in 1955, and was a board member of the Buddhistische Gesellschaft Hamburg (1954).

Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar Paul Demiéville studied at the Sorbonne and under scholars including Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at Xiamen University, Maison Franco-Japonaise, INALCO, EPHE (1945–1957), and the Collège de France (1946–1964).

Indologist and philosopher Paul Deussen studied at Bonn, Tübingen, and Humboldt University of Berlin, completing his habilitation under Eduard Zeller. He taught at Geneva, Humboldt University of Berlin (1881–1887), and held a professorship at Kiel University from 1889.

Indologist and religious studies scholar Paul Dundas studied at Edinburgh under Michael Coulson and at Cambridge under John Brough and K. R. Norman. He led Asian studies at the University of Edinburgh from 1976 and also led the Pali Text Society.

Paul E. Muller-Ortega is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed doctoral studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara. He is attested teaching in the Department of Religion and Classics at the University of Rochester in 2000.
Paul Ekman studied at New York University (~1952–1954) and Adelphi University (~1954–1958). He served on the faculty of the University of California, San Francisco, from circa 1960 to 2004.

Paul F. Knitter is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed studies at the Pontifical Gregorian University (~1958–1966) and the University of Marburg (~1970–1972), later holding a post at Union Theological Seminary around 2007.

Historian Paul Fredericq studied at Ghent University and the University of Liège. He served as professor at the University of Liège (~1879–1884), and at Ghent University from 1883, where he became rector in 1919.

Paul Fuller is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated under Paul Dundas and Rupert Gethin, he earned his PhD from the University of Bristol (2003) and taught at the University of Sydney, Cardiff University, and the University of Edinburgh.

Indologist Paul G. Brewster studied at Oakland City University and the University of Oklahoma. He held teaching posts at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, UNC Chapel Hill, Shurtleff College, Henderson State University, and Tennessee Technological University (1954).

Paul G. Hackett specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as South Asia Bibliographer and Tibetan collection curator at the University of Virginia (attested 1994, 2003) and as Lecturer in Classical Tibetan at Columbia University (attested 2003–2016).

Indologist and linguist Paul Goldschmidt studied at Heidelberg, Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, Berlin under Albrecht Weber, and Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. In 1874, he was appointed epigraphist and Commissioner of Archaeology for the Government of Ceylon.
Historian and Indologist Paul Greenough earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (1968–1977). He joined the history faculty at the University of Iowa in 1974.

Paul Groner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and earned his PhD at Yale. Since at least 1982, he has been a religious studies faculty member at the University of Virginia.

Indologist and philosopher Paul Hacker earned his PhD at Berlin and completed his habilitation at Bonn under Willibald Kirfel. He held professorships at the Mithila Institute (1954–1955), the University of Bonn (1955–1963), and the University of Münster (1963–1978).

Paul Harrison is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Auckland and the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong. His career includes posts at Auckland, the University of Canterbury, and Stanford University.

Paul Hershman was an Indology scholar who undertook doctoral studies at the London School of Economics (~1971–1975). He was appointed Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Sussex, serving from circa 1975 to 1976.
Paul Hoornaert is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. His career includes posts at Kanazawa University, where he is attested as a lecturer in 1991 and on faculty in 2002.
